evidence: backend/servers/api-server/src/routes/ai/llm.rs:1119-1158 — `enhanced_chat` is a stubbed production handler that returns fabricated data. It ignores the request except to echo it: `"response": format!("I understand you're asking about: {}. Let me help you with that.", req.message)` (line 1149), with a hardcoded `confidence: 0.85` (line 1144), `tokens_used: 150`, empty `sources: []`, and an `escalated` flag derived from the fake confidence. No LLM call, no document-embedding search is performed. The inline comment admits it: `// Placeholder response - real implementation would: 1. Search document embeddings ... 2. Call LLM with context ... 3. Check confidence against threshold`.

Reachable in production: mounted at POST /chat/enhanced in `llm_router()` (backend/servers/api-server/src/routes/ai/llm.rs:49, `.route("/chat/enhanced", post(enhanced_chat))`), which lib.rs wires into the app. The placeholder branch is unconditional — every caller receives the canned echo plus fabricated confidence/token/escalation metrics, so any UI or client that trusts these fields is acting on invented data.

Fix: implement the documented pipeline (embedding search -> LLM call -> confidence/escalation check) or fail closed with a 501/NOT_IMPLEMENTED instead of returning a success payload with fabricated confidence and token counts. The neighbouring `generate_lease` handler in the same file shows the real LLM-call + persistence pattern to follow.

backend/servers/api-server/src/routes/ai/llm.rs:687 — the raw upstream LLM-provider error is forwarded verbatim into the client-facing response body: `Json(ErrorResponse::new("GENERATION_FAILED", format!("Failed to generate lease: {}", e)))`. The error is already captured server-side via `tracing::error!("Lease generation failed: {}", e)` (line 658), so the client copy adds no user value while potentially exposing provider request IDs, model/config hints, or fragments of the upstream response body.

backend/servers/api-server/src/routes/ai/voice.rs:194 — same pattern on the voice OAuth path: `Json(ErrorResponse::new("OAUTH_EXCHANGE_FAILED", format!("Failed to exchange authorization code: {}", e)))` returns the upstream OAuth-provider exchange error `e` (already logged at voice.rs:189) directly to the API caller.

This is a segment-level error-hygiene pattern: internal/upstream error detail should be logged server-side (as it already is) and replaced with a generic client message. Fix: return a stable generic message (e.g. "Lease generation failed", "Authorization code exchange failed") and keep the detailed `{e}` only in the tracing call.

frontend/apps/mobile/src/contexts/AuthContext.tsx:85-95 — the cold-start `initialize()` effect reads the stored access token (`SecureStore.getItemAsync(ACCESS_TOKEN_KEY)`) and, whenever both `accessToken` and `userJson` are present, unconditionally sets `{ isLoading:false, isAuthenticated:true, user, accessToken }`. It never decodes/checks the token's `exp` claim and never calls the existing `refreshToken()`. Because access tokens are short-lived (refresh tokens are the long-lived credential — see REFRESH_TOKEN_KEY / the /auth/refresh flow at :209-231), any app cold-start that happens after the stored access token's TTL has elapsed restores the user into an `isAuthenticated:true` state holding an already-expired bearer token.

frontend/apps/mobile/src/contexts/AuthContext.tsx:296-312 — `authenticateWithBiometric` has the identical gap on the unlock path: after `LocalAuthentication.authenticateAsync` succeeds it reads the stored `accessToken`/`userJson` and sets `isAuthenticated:true` with that token, with an explicit comment (":296") that it deliberately does NOT refetch/reset (issue #2399) — but it also performs no `exp` validation and no proactive `refreshToken()`, so a biometric unlock after the access token expired lands the user authenticated-but-with-an-expired-token.

This compounds the already-filed `code-review-mobile-rn-useapi-no-refresh-retry` (the API layer does not transparently refresh + retry on 401): with no proactive refresh at restore/unlock AND no reactive refresh-retry in useApi, the first request after an expired restore 401s and the user is stuck in a broken 'logged in but everything fails' state until a manual logout/login. `refreshToken()` already exists in this same context (:209) and is simply never invoked on the two restore paths. Fix: on `initialize()` and on successful biometric unlock, decode the access token's `exp` (utils/jwt.ts already ships a guarded `decodeJwtPayload`) and, if expired/near-expiry, `await refreshToken()` before setting `isAuthenticated:true` (fall back to the login screen if refresh fails).

frontend/apps/mobile/src/contexts/AuthContext.tsx:252-256 — `enableBiometric` passes hardcoded English strings to the OS biometric dialog: `promptMessage: 'Enable biometric login'`, `cancelLabel: 'Cancel'`, `fallbackLabel: 'Use passcode'`. None are wrapped in `t()`, so non-English users (this app ships sk/cs/de/en) see English in the native Face ID / fingerprint prompt.

frontend/apps/mobile/src/contexts/AuthContext.tsx:284-287 — `authenticateWithBiometric` repeats it: `promptMessage: 'Login to Property Management'`, `cancelLabel: 'Cancel'`, `fallbackLabel: 'Use password'` — all hardcoded English on the unlock prompt.

Fix: route these six strings through `t('auth.biometric.*')` keys so the login/unlock prompts localise with the rest of the app.

frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/lib/websocket.ts:688-709 — the client heartbeat sends an APPLICATION-level ping frame `{type:'ping', payload:null, timestamp}` via send() every heartbeatInterval (default 30000ms, :288), sets `awaitingPong = true`, and arms a pongTimeout (default 10000ms, :289). The ONLY thing that clears awaitingPong is receiving a text frame whose `data.type === 'pong'` (handleMessage :529-532 -> handlePong :711-718). If no such frame arrives within 10s, `this.socket?.close(4000, 'Pong timeout')` fires (:705), producing a non-clean close -> onclose (:495-510) -> scheduleReconnect().

The api-server notification WS handler NEVER sends an application-level `{type:'pong'}`. Verified in backend/servers/api-server/src/routes/ws_notifications.rs: the server only emits `Message::Text` carrying the `{event, payload}` WsEvent envelope (:219-230) for notifications, and uses PROTOCOL-level `Message::Ping(vec![])` for its own liveness probe (:242). Its inbound arm (:257-260) explicitly treats every client frame (Text/Binary/Ping/Pong) as a heartbeat and returns without replying — see the module header comment (:27, 'Client -> server: any message is treated as a heartbeat (pong)'). No code path serialises the string 'pong' back to the client.

Consequence: on every connection the client opens (onopen -> startHeartbeat :488-493), 30s later it sends `{type:'ping'}`, the server swallows it, awaitingPong stays true, and at ~40s the client force-closes with code 4000 and reconnects. onclose->stopHeartbeat->scheduleReconnect->connect->onopen->startHeartbeat repeats the cycle indefinitely. parseServerMessage (:59-76) maps real notification events onto `type = <event name>`, never 'pong', so an incoming notification never clears awaitingPong either. The realtime notification channel therefore drops and reconnects roughly every 40s for the entire authenticated session.

Reachability confirmed in production: App.tsx:94-101 mounts <WebSocketProvider> around the whole authenticated app with NO heartbeatInterval/pongTimeout override, so the 30s/10s defaults apply; WebSocketContext.tsx:250-251 calls service.connect() whenever auth.isAuthenticated && accessToken. Impact: constant socket churn, missed pushes during each reconnect gap, redundant server WS-session setup/teardown, and spurious onDisconnected/onReconnected callback firing every ~40s. Fix: the client-side app-level ping is both wrong (server never answers it) and redundant (the server already pings and the browser auto-pongs at the protocol level, invisible to JS). Remove the sendPing/pongTimeout logic and rely on the server's Message::Ping + browser auto-pong for liveness; OR have the server echo an application `{type:'pong'}` on receipt of `{type:'ping'}` so the contract matches. Distinct from the prior ws-token-rotation-stale and ws-ungated-console findings.

frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/lib/websocket.ts:600-612 — once reconnectAttempts reaches maxReconnectAttempts (default 10, :290) scheduleReconnect() sets `shouldReconnect = false`, emits `connection:max-retries-exceeded`, and sets an error state. From that point NOTHING in the client re-arms reconnection: onclose only reconnects when shouldReconnect is true (:507), and reconnectAttempts is never reset by connect() or disconnect() — only a successful onopen resets it (:489). The public resetReconnectAttempts() (:479-481) is dead code (no caller in the segment).

The default backoff sum (min 1000ms doubling, capped at 30000ms, over 10 attempts) is only ~3 minutes, so any real outage longer than that — laptop sleep, tunnel/VPN drop, backend redeploy window, mobile network gap — permanently kills the notification socket for the rest of the session.

There is no auto-resume wiring. contexts/WebSocketContext.tsx only calls service.connect() on an auth change (:246-256); it never subscribes to `connection:max-retries-exceeded` and is not connected to hooks/useNetworkStatus.ts (which already detects browser online/offline transitions, useNetworkStatus.ts:96-121). So when connectivity returns, the socket stays dead until the user logs out/in or reloads the page — user silently stops receiving realtime pushes with no indication and no recovery path.

Fix: on the browser `online` event (or via useNetworkStatusEffect) call service.connect() to resume, and have connect() reset reconnectAttempts (or call resetReconnectAttempts()) so a fresh attempt budget is granted; optionally surface the `connection:max-retries-exceeded` state in WebSocketContext so the UI can offer a manual reconnect. Net-new — no prior ppt-web-core finding covered the reconnect give-up / resume lifecycle.
